text: **Engramory**（DSH 插件及多宿主记忆工具）：把重要信息存为普通 Markdown 笔记，并在会话开始时注入只含链接的限长索引，需要细节时再打开对应文档。笔记可直接阅读和编辑，不依赖数据库或向量服务；DSH 插件提供自动索引、记忆管理侧栏及写入检查。一个 Agent 可负责写入，其他宿主只读同一记忆库。适合希望跨会话保留偏好、项目事实和可复用经验的用户。

**Engramory** (DSH memory plugin): Save knowledge as readable Markdown notes with a compact index loaded at session start. Open details when needed; no database or vector service. Includes a DSH memory sidebar and supports shared read access from other hosts.

**Engramory** 的功能「markdown-memory」：将重要信息分别保存为可读 Markdown 笔记，并在 MEMORY.md 索引中以链接和简短摘要列出，方便按需查阅。
**Engramory** 的功能「session-injection」：在会话开始时将限长记忆索引加入上下文，Agent 需要具体信息时再打开对应笔记。
**Engramory** 的功能「dsh-sidebar」：在 DSH 中提供记忆侧栏，查看记忆条目并调整记忆库位置。
**Engramory** 的功能「shared-read-store」：支持一个宿主负责写记忆，其他宿主以只读方式访问同一目录中的笔记库。
**Engramory** 的功能「memory-maintenance」：提供索引检查与记忆库诊断工具，帮助维护条目链接和库结构。

**Agent 通用长期记忆层。** AI 记住的东西存成一个个普通 markdown 文件，一个只放指针的索引 `MEMORY.md` 列出全部笔记，每次会话开头读进来，细节要用时再打开。不需要数据库、向量或服务器，文件你能直接看、能改。Claude Code、Codex、[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)（dsh）、OpenClaw、Kiro 等都能用；一个工具负责写，别的工具可以只读同一个库。

dsh-engramory README · Engramory：**dsh 有专用插件** `dsh-engramory`：装上就能用，自动带上索引，把索引写超上限的写入大多在落盘前就被拦下，侧栏还多一个记忆页。Claude Code 用 hook 拦超限写入；其他工具靠规则加校验脚本。

> 名字来自 *engram*（记忆痕迹）+ *memory*。本项目是 `tinqiao-oss/engramory`（dsh 插件的 npm 包叫 `dsh-engramory`），与其他所有者名下的同名仓库无关。

```sh
section: 让另一个 AI 只读同一个库

text:
dsh-engramory README · Claude Code：写进用户级的 ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md，每个项目都读得到：python tools/engramory_init.py claude-reader --project-root ~/.claude \
  --memory-root ~/.dsh/.engramory-memory

dsh-engramory README · Codex：写进 ~/.codex/AGENTS.md：python tools/engramory_init.py codex-reader --project-root ~/.codex \
  --memory-root ~/.dsh/.engramory-memory
```

dsh 插件给全局库换过位置的，`--memory-root` 写换过之后的位置；以后再换，读者要用新位置重装一次。

反过来让 dsh 读 Claude Code 的库，换成 `dsh-reader`，`--memory-root` 指向 `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory`。

读者不建库，`--memory-root` 里必须已有 `MEMORY.md`。读者自己的记忆照旧：Claude Code 读着 dsh 的库，你跟它说「记住……」，它记进自己的库，dsh 看不到。想让两边都知道，就各写各的库、互相只读对方的。"只读"靠规则约束，不是强制的；回忆到的内容会发给那个宿主的模型服务商。详见[读取器指南](adapters/reader/README.md)。

dsh-engramory README · 为什么这样做：- **索引小，细节按需打开。** 索引每次会话开头都要读进来（宿主自动注入，比如 dsh 插件；或者由 AI 自己读），所以只放指针，默认上限 200 行 / 25 KB。
- **笔记要整理，不是堆日志。** 四种类型 `user | feedback | project | reference`。写之前查重，能更新旧笔记就不新建，过时的删掉或归档，git 和代码里已有的不重复记。陪伴角色另有 `moment`（经历）、`upcoming`（约定）、`self`（我自己）三类（[SKILL.md](SKILL.md) §2.2）；记忆库可以用中文写（§1.1）。
- **写入前卡上限。** 在 dsh（插件）和 Claude Code（hook）上，算得出结果、会把索引写超上限的写入，在写入前就被拒绝，压缩照样放行。其他工具靠规则加校验脚本。
- **任务续接不另建交接库。** 没做完的任务只留一条 `project` 笔记，就地更新状态和下一步；compact、清空或开新线程前做一次[续接同步](PORTING.md#3-wire-continuity-sync--explicit-first-hooks-optional)。

dsh-engramory README · 和别的方案比：- **原生记忆**（如 Claude Code auto-memory）：同样是索引加详情文件；Engramory 多了明确的整理规则和写前上限。
- **检索和自动捕获系统**（basic-memory、mem0、Zep、agentmemory 等）：面向大量记忆；Engramory 不做搜索和自动摄取，只管人工精选的个人记忆。
- **不做 MCP server。** 对能读写文件、能加载常驻规则的宿主，MCP 会多出一条绕过写前上限的写入通道，还会把"每次都加载的索引"降级成"模型得记得去调用的工具"。两样都没有的宿主，可以把 MCP 当补充入口。

dsh-engramory README · 卸载：dsh 插件：`dsh plugin --profile <名字> remove dsh-engramory`。用安装脚本装的，用安装时的宿主和路径再跑一次，加 `--uninstall`（先加 `--dry-run` 看计划）：

```sh
python tools/engramory_init.py codex --uninstall
```

只删安装器自己的东西：规则块、skill 副本、Codex hook。**记忆库永远不删**，真想清空请自己删。

dsh-engramory README · 安全与隐私：记忆库是**未加密的明文**，本机进程都能读；`.gitignore` 只管 git，云同步、备份照样会复制它。

- **永远不存密码、key、token、cookie 的值**，只记它们在哪（密码管理器、环境变量名）。
- 手机号、邮箱、地址这类个人信息少存，尽量只记指针。

没有自动扫描，全靠纪律。见 [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) §5/§8 和 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)。

dsh-engramory README · 版本规则：仓库的 `vX.Y.Z` 和 npm 包 `dsh-engramory@X.Y.Z` 是同一次发布，只改了一边也一起发（[CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) 写明改了哪边）。

**只在主版本做不兼容改动：**

- **记忆库格式：** 目录结构（`MEMORY.md`、一条笔记一个文件、`archive/`）、frontmatter 字段、四种类型及各自的必填项、索引的标题和指针行，中英文都算。
- **工具：** `tools/` 下脚本的命令和参数（包括 `engramory_init.py` 把库建在哪），以及 Claude Code、Codex 的 hook。
- **dsh 插件：** 包名、上限判定，以及 `indexName`、`maxLines`、`maxBytes`、`indexPath`、`registerSkill`、`injectIndex`、`language`、`skill` 这些配置。

**实验性，小版本也可能改：** 大肥鱼模式（`companion`）和它的三种类型、社交模式（`audience`）、插件的设置页和记忆页。
dsh-engramory README · 版本规则：协议措辞每次发布都可能修订，但会让合格的记忆库变得不合格的规则要等主版本。记忆库不带版本号，格式变了的迁移步骤写在 CHANGELOG。安全修复可能在任何版本改变不安全配置的行为，CHANGELOG 会写明。

dsh-engramory README · 已知局限：- **只有 dsh 和 Claude Code 有写前拒绝**，而且 shell、MCP 文件工具、外部编辑器都能绕过。其他宿主只靠规则，尽力而为；各宿主的情况以 [PORTING.md](PORTING.md) 为准。
- **整理靠模型自觉遵守规则**，不是强制的。
- **没有来源、可信度、过期字段。** 回忆到的内容只供参考，可能被人为影响（[SKILL.md](SKILL.md) §4）。
- **没有项目 ID。** 多个项目共用一个库时，笔记名可能撞、内容可能串。
- **一个库只能有一个写入者**，见[单写者、多读者](adapters/reader/README.md)。
- **只适合个人规模。** 活跃记忆要装得进有界的索引；大量资料请用检索系统。

dsh-engramory README · Engramory：**A general-purpose long-term memory layer for AI agents.** What the AI remembers is kept as small markdown
files, one per memory, with a pointer-only index (`MEMORY.md`) that is read at the start
of every session; a note is opened when its details are needed. No database,
embeddings, or server; you can read and edit every file yourself. It works with Claude
Code, Codex, [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh),
OpenClaw, Kiro and others; one agent writes a store, and others can read it.

dsh-engramory README · Engramory：**dsh has a dedicated plugin**, `dsh-engramory`: it works once installed, brings the
index into the conversation, refuses most writes that would grow the index past
its cap before they land, and adds a Memory page to the sidebar. On Claude Code a hook
refuses those writes; other tools rely on the rules plus a checker.

dsh-engramory README · Engramory：> The name is *engram* (a memory's physical trace) + *memory*. This project is
> `tinqiao-oss/engramory` (the dsh plugin is `dsh-engramory` on npm); same-named
> repositories under other owners are unrelated.

([one writer, many readers](adapters/reader/README.md)). Say the dsh plugin writes its
global store, and Claude Code and Codex read it:

```sh
section: Let another agent read the same store

text:
dsh-engramory README · Claude Code: into the user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, which every project loads：python tools/engramory_init.py claude-reader --project-root ~/.claude \
  --memory-root ~/.dsh/.engramory-memory
section: Claude Code: into the user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, which every project loads

text:
dsh-engramory README · Codex: into ~/.codex/AGENTS.md：python tools/engramory_init.py codex-reader --project-root ~/.codex \
  --memory-root ~/.dsh/.engramory-memory
```

Where the dsh plugin has moved its global store, `--memory-root` is where it is now; move it
again, and install the readers again with the new place.

The other way round, dsh reading Claude Code's store, is `dsh-reader` with
`--memory-root ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory`.

dsh-engramory README · Codex: into ~/.codex/AGENTS.md：A reader creates no store; `--memory-root` must already hold a `MEMORY.md`. A reader
keeps its own memory: Claude Code reading the dsh store still files what you tell it to
remember in its own store, which dsh does not see. For both to know, let each write its
own store and read the other's. "Read-only" is a rule the agent follows, not enforced,
and what it recalls goes to that host's model provider. See the
[reader guide](adapters/reader/README.md).

dsh-engramory README · Why it works this way：- **A small index, details on demand.** The index is read at the start of every
  session (injected by the host, as the dsh plugin does, or read by the agent), so it holds
  pointers only, capped at 200 lines / 25 KB by default.
- **Curated notes, not a log.** Four types: `user | feedback | project | reference`.
  Before writing, the agent checks for a duplicate, updates an existing note rather
  than adding one, retires what is stale, and does not copy what git or the code
  already records. A companion character adds `moment`, `upcoming` and `self` for its
  own life ([SKILL.md](SKILL.md) §2.2); a store can be written in Chinese (§1.1).
- **The cap is enforced before the write.** On dsh (a plugin) and Claude Code (a hook),
  a write whose result can be worked out and would grow the index past the cap is
  refused before it lands; compaction still passes. Other tools rely on the rules plus
  a checker.
- **Continuity without a handoff store.** An unfinished task keeps one `project` note,
  updated in place with its status and next step; before a compact, clear, or new
  thread, the agent runs a [continuity sync](PORTING.md#3-wire-contin

dsh-engramory README · How it compares：- **Native memory** (such as Claude Code auto-memory): the same index-plus-files
  pattern; Engramory adds explicit curation rules and a pre-write cap.
- **Retrieval and auto-capture systems** (basic-memory, mem0, Zep, agentmemory, …):
  built for large memory sets. Engramory has no search engine or automatic ingestion;
  it is for a curated personal set.
- **No MCP server.** For a host that already reads files and loads standing rules, MCP
  would open a second write channel past the pre-write cap, and turn recall from an
  index loaded every session into a tool the model has to remember to call. For a host
  with neither, an MCP entry point is worth adding as a supplement.

dsh-engramory README · Uninstall：The dsh plugin: `dsh plugin --profile <name> remove dsh-engramory`. For a setup made
with the installer, run the same host and paths again with `--uninstall` (add
`--dry-run` first to see the plan):

```sh
python tools/engramory_init.py codex --uninstall
```

It removes only what the installer put there: the rules block, the skill copy, the
Codex hooks. **The memory store is never removed**; delete it yourself if you want it
gone.

dsh-engramory README · Security & privacy：The store is **plain, unencrypted text** that any local process can read; `.gitignore`
only keeps it out of git, and cloud sync or backups still copy it.

- **Never store secret values** (keys, tokens, passwords, cookies), only where they
  live (a password manager, an environment variable's name).
- Keep personal details such as phone numbers, email or addresses to a minimum; prefer
  pointers.

dsh-engramory README · Security & privacy：Nothing scans for secrets; it is discipline only. See [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) §5/§8 and
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

dsh-engramory README · Versioning：The repo's `vX.Y.Z` and the npm package `dsh-engramory@X.Y.Z` are one release,
published together even when only one side changed (the [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) says
which).

**Change incompatibly only in a major version:**

dsh-engramory README · Versioning：- **The store format:** the layout (`MEMORY.md`, one note per file, `archive/`), the
  frontmatter keys, the four types and what each requires, and the index's headings and
  pointer lines, in English and in Chinese.
- **The tools:** the scripts in `tools/` (their commands and options, and where
  `engramory_init.py` puts a store), and the Claude Code and Codex hooks.
- **The dsh plugin:** its package name, the cap's decisions, and the settings
  `indexName`, `maxLines`, `maxBytes`, `indexPath`, `registerSkill`, `injectIndex`,
  `language` and `skill`.

dsh-engramory README · Versioning：**Experimental, may change in a minor version:** companion mode (`companion`) and its
three types, social mode (`audience`), and the plugin's settings and memory pages.

The protocol's wording is revised in any release, but a rule that would make a valid
store invalid waits for a major version. The store carries no version number; a format
change's migration steps go in the CHANGELOG. A security fix may change what an unsafe
configuration does in any release, and the CHANGELOG says so.

dsh-engramory README · Known limitations：- **Only dsh and Claude Code refuse a write before it lands**, and shell tools, MCP
  file tools and external editors go past both. Every other host relies on the rules,
  best-effort; [PORTING.md](PORTING.md) is the authoritative host picture.
- **Curation depends on the model following the rules**; nothing enforces it.
- **No provenance, confidence or expiry fields.** Recalled memory is advisory and can
  be influenced by an attacker ([SKILL.md](SKILL.md) §4).
- **No project ID.** Projects sharing one store can collide on note names or bleed
  into each other.
- **One writer per store**; see [one writer, many readers](adapters/reader/README.md).
- **Personal scale only.** The active set must fit the bounded index; for a large
  corpus use a retrieval system.
